If the model above represents $4$ wholes, use the model to solve the following division problem. Express your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

$4÷\frac{3}{4}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To calculate $4÷\frac{3}{4}$, we first need to divide each of the $4$ wholes into $4$ equal parts.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/137a7924f2a2f463a014b3d6e289cc386b7981856febb02f5a1f7f7454e8ea1f.png)

 

Next, we break this into groups of $3$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/a569b682856cef52674f2fd517577c04a543a3ba385c6d904ec2955c9f792f53.png)

 

Note the following: 

- We got $\boxed{\text{5}}$ full groups.

- There is $1$ part left over out of a possible group of $3.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\frac{1}{3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
4÷\frac{3}{4}=\boxed{\text{5}}\,\frac{1}{3}.
$$
